title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Σ = P^1(C) carries complex conjugation τ, and Σ* = U_{0,3} = P^1 \ {0,1,∞}. On the previous page Grothendieck showed the following. Weighted (not necessarily orientable, 'bi-maillées') maps of type {0,1,∞} form a full subcategory of the finite 'mixed' {1,τ}-coverings of U_{0,3}. These are topological coverings X' → Σ, étale over U_{0,3}, with an involution τ_{X'} lifting conjugation. The subcategory is cut out by condition (25): X'^τ = ∅, meaning τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ act without fixed points. In map terms, X' is the orientation double cover of the map and τ_{X'} is orientation reversal.

This page.
(i) Descent. A ramified covering of Σ, étale over U_{0,3}, together with a compatible {1,τ}-action, is the same as a covering of the C-scheme P^1_C (via Riemann existence / GAGA) plus a descent datum from C to R. By Galois descent along Spec C → Spec R, this is the same as a finite cover of the R-scheme P^1_R that is étale over U_{0,3,R} = P^1_R \ {0,1,∞}. So the category of mixed coverings is equivalent to the category of finite étale covers of the real scheme P^1_R \ {0,1,∞}, or equivalently of their normal completions over P^1_R.
(ii) The functor (26). Composing gives a canonical fully faithful functor: finite weighted triangular maps of type {0,1,∞} → finite étale covers of P^1_R \ {0,1,∞}.
(iii) Essential image. It consists of the X' with no real points, condition (27): X'(R) = ∅. This merely restates (25), since X'(R) = X'(C)^τ.
(iv) Inverse functor. Take X'(C) and the preimage of the real line P^1(R) ⊂ Σ. This gives an oriented triangulation whose vertices are partitioned into three classes, the fibres over 0, 1 and ∞. Then pass to the quotient by conjugation.
(v) Continuation on the next page. Under (27) the quotient X'(C)/τ is a closed, possibly non-orientable surface carrying the map. Without (27) it is a compact surface with boundary carrying a dianalytic (Klein) structure. Extending the notion of map to surfaces with boundary makes (26) an equivalence of categories.

Purpose. This is the real / non-orientable version of the dessins ↔ Belyi-curves dictionary, inside the 'Teichmülleries' study of maps and the action of Galois groups (here Gal(C/R) = {1,τ}).
errors: Minor slip: the text says 'rev. ramifié X' de X'; it should read 'of Σ = P^1_C'.

Implicit point, not an error: if X' is geometrically disconnected over R (e.g. a C-curve viewed as an R-scheme), then X'(R) = ∅ automatically and the quotient is the orientable map. This is consistent with orientable maps sitting inside non-oriented ones, but Grothendieck does not state it.

The claim that X'^τ is empty iff its trace over U' is empty (previous page) is correct. The fixed locus of an antiholomorphic involution on a compact Riemann surface is a disjoint union of circles, never isolated points, so any nonempty fixed locus meets the dense open U'.

ideas.what: Galois descent C/R identifies {1,τ}-equivariant ramified covers of P^1(C) étale over U_{0,3} with finite covers of the R-scheme P^1_R étale over P^1_R minus {0,1,∞}
ideas.modern_name: Real Riemann existence theorem / Galois descent for real algebraic curves (Klein surfaces ↔ real curves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein; Alling–Greenleaf 1971 for Klein surfaces ↔ real function fields)
ideas.where_published: Descent formalism in SGA1 / FGA; the specific real statement possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Fully faithful functor from (non-orientable) weighted triangular maps to finite étale covers of P^1_R \ {0,1,∞}, with essential image the covers having no real points
ideas.modern_name: Real Belyi theory: non-orientable dessins ↔ real Belyi pairs without real points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Köck–Singerman, 'Real Belyi theory' (2007); Bryant–Singerman (non-orientable maps, 1985); Jones–Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions non-orientable maps / surfaces with boundary only briefly, if at all — unsure

ideas.what: Extending maps to compact surfaces with boundary (quotient X'(C)/τ when real points exist) to make the functor an equivalence
ideas.modern_name: Dessins on Klein surfaces with boundary ↔ real Belyi functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Köck–Singerman 2007; Bujalance et al. on Klein surfaces

ideas.what: Recovering the triangulation from the preimage of P^1(R), with vertex 3-colouring by the fibres over 0, 1, ∞
ideas.modern_name: Clean triangulation / 'black-white-star' triangulation associated with a Belyi map (Grothendieck–Voevodsky–Shabat, Cohen–Itzykson–Wolfart)

missed.claim: Already in 1981–82 Grothendieck had a precise real Belyi theory. Non-orientable weighted triangular maps of type {0,1,∞} embed fully faithfully into finite étale covers of P^1_R minus {0,1,∞}, with essential image exactly the X' with X'(R) = ∅. Maps on surfaces with boundary (next page) give the full equivalence. This is usually credited to Singerman and coauthors (Köck–Singerman 2007), apparently without reference to these notes.
missed.quote: On trouve ainsi un foncteur pleinement fidèle canonique (26) cartes triangulaires finies pondérées de type {0,1,∞} → revêtements finis étales du schéma P^1_R \ {0,1,∞} ... L'image essentielle est formée des rev. X' tels que (27) X'(R) = ∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for real Belyi theory. The clean characterisation 'no real points ⇔ closed non-orientable map' is the key lemma of Köck–Singerman, so the attribution record is incomplete.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a fairly direct descent argument, and the result was later independently established (Köck–Singerman's real Belyi theory). Its notable feature is the early, clean, functorial formulation by Grothendieck, including the essential-image criterion X'(R) = ∅ and the boundary extension. This is historically interesting, but not something a specialist would find mathematically surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'interprétation qui ne fait que traduire (26)[?]' should read 'traduire (25)': it refers back to condition (25) X'^τ = ∅ from the previous page.
The underbrace note reads 'noté X' dans (25)' rather than 'soit X' dans (26)'.
'à rev. ramifié X' de X' — the X is a bold symbol, most likely standing for Σ.
